text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- Croatia is proposing to U.N. transitional administrator Jacques Klein that the reconstruction of Eastern Slavonia start as early as March.

- The government to offer a 70 million kuna loan for cattle producers at a favourable 9.0-percent rate. The aim of the move is to ensure sufficient quantities of meat products for the oncoming tourist season.
- Croatian tourism could in the future turn to developing private accommodation rather than big hotels, as there is more money to be made that way.
- Some 7,400 citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina, 3,066 Yugoslav nationals, 2,999 Romanians, 478 Turks and 211 Ukrainians have tried to illegally enter Croatia during 1996.

- The rise in the cost of life for the citizens of Zagreb in January has been put at 2.7 percent and of retail prices at 1.3 percent compared to December 1996, this according to the city statistics bureau. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
